title: Nonlinear Optics Mediated by Chiral Waveguide QED: Generation of Momentum-anticorrelated Photon Pairs
authors: Wenqi Tong, Spencer J Walsh, H. Alaeian, F. Robicheaux
abstract: In recent years, chiral quantum optics has emerged as an active research area due to the promising applications in quantum information processing as well as nonlinear optics. We present results on the properties of the incoherent component of the transmitted light after transmons chirally coupled to a waveguide. The well-known resonance fluorescence of one chiral transmon resembles nonlinear quantum optics as it can convert the coherent light, with photons having spatially extensive coherence and Poisson distribution, into a field with spatially localized coherence and bunching photon statistics. However, another chiral transmon can undo the effect of the first transmon regardless of the Rabi frequency under the idealization involved in this work. A full wavefunction calculation shows that, in the weak driving limit, this incoherent light mainly comes from two-photon processes - one chiral transmon converts two independent photons into a photon pair with opposite momentum shift. In addition to the driving through the waveguide, a local driving with independently tunable amplitude and phase can address each transmon individually. The interplay between the waveguide driving and local driving modulates the contribution of the incoherent transmission and hence enables the engineering of the quantum statistics of the transmitted field, with tunable $g^{(2)}(0)$ spanning anti-bunched, coherent, and strongly bunched regimes.
summary: This paper explores how chiral coupling between transmons and a waveguide can mediate nonlinear quantum optical effects to generate momentum-anticorrelated photon pairs. By combining waveguide driving with independently tunable local drives, the researchers demonstrate precise control over the transmitted light's quantum statistics, tuning it from anti-bunched to super-bunched regimes.
main_problem: The research investigates nonlinear optics mediated by chiral waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) to achieve the generation of momentum-anticorrelated photon pairs.
main_result: The interplay between waveguide driving and local driving allows for the engineering of quantum statistics in the transmitted field, enabling tunable control over $g^{(2)}(0)$ across anti-bunched, coherent, and strongly bunched regimes.
method: The study employs both semi-classical simulations (using input-output theory) and full quantum wavefunction calculations to analyze light transmission through coupled transmon qubits.
model_or_system: The system consists of multiple transmons (superconducting qubits) chirally coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating local driving, waveguide coupling, and dissipation via a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Second-order correlation function ($g^{(2)}(0)$), coherent transmission amplitude ($\langle\hat{\alpha}angle$), and the power spectrum density of the incoherent component.
important_parameters: Rabi frequencies ($\Omega_{wg}, \Omega_d$), detunings ($\Delta_n$), and the coupling strength ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes $\hbar=1$, perfect coupling efficiency, and utilizes approximations like Born-Markov for some simulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the system setup (transmons coupled to a waveguide) and show quantitative results such as $T_{inc}$ vs. Rabi frequency, power spectra of the incoherent component, and $g^{(2)}(	au)$ confirming bunching behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical model (Hamiltonian/Master Equation) to analyzing coherent transmission via input-output theory, then detailing how single or multiple chiral transmons modify photon statistics by generating an incoherent component, which can be controlled using local driving fields.
why_interesting: This work bridges superconducting circuit QED with quantum optics concepts like nonlinear light generation and photon correlation engineering, providing a platform for realizing complex quantum optical phenomena in solid-state systems.
